title: Soft Eviction Windows and KV Reuse Degradation Playbook
content:
Purpose
This note captures an exploratory investigation into "soft eviction windows" for KV cache entries — a configurable grace period before entries become eligible for eviction — and the effect of this policy on reuse rates, paging, and memory-bandwidth-driven tail latency under bursty workloads. Goal: pragmatic recommendations (and a small runbook) for a conservative soft-eviction rollout that reduces pageback storms without materially hurting steady-state hit-rate or unit cost.

Background / motivation
We see recurring latency tails when multi-tenant bursts coincide with tight memory residency budgets. Classic eviction-on-threshold (hard eviction) aggressively removes entries as soon as residency targets are exceeded, which reduces hit-rate immediately and can amplify downstream paging and NVMe writeback bursts. Hypothesis: inserting a short, activity-driven grace window (soft eviction) can absorb transient bursts of working-set pressure and preserve reuse for entries with imminent reuse, trading small memory headroom for fewer pagebacks and smoother bandwidth.

Key definitions used in this note
- soft_eviction_window (ms): time after an entry crosses eviction-priority threshold during which it is exempt from eviction unless explicitly pinned/overruled.
- degradation_factor: relative drop in reuse-rate (fraction) when soft windows are too large for constrained-memory regimes.
- pageback_storm: a transient spike in NVMe IO and DMA stalls correlated with simultaneous evictions across many partitions.
- reuse_signal: a moving-window metric (per entry class) that weights last-access recency and frequency to estimate imminent touch probability.

Experiment design summary
Hardware: 8x A100 nodes (local lab), NVMe-backed host swap configured on node-level. Same host image used for all runs.
Workload: synthetic mix derived from production traces (sampled 72h), two classes: chat (high sequential KV reuse) and embed+search (random-ish KV reads). Mix proportions: 70% chat, 30% embed.
Configs compared (single run series for each):
- baseline_hard: current policy (LRU-ish eviction, immediate eligibility when residency > threshold).
- soft-50ms: soft_eviction_window = 50ms + reuse_signal gating.
- soft-200ms: soft_eviction_window = 200ms + reuse_signal gating.
- soft-adaptive: window = base 20ms, extended up to 500ms under detected burst smoothing mode (algorithm described below).
Metrics captured:
- reuse_rate: fraction of lookups that hit KV (per-token basis).
- eviction_rate: evictions/sec per device.
- pageback_iops and average NVMe latency.
- P95 token-response latency and P99 tail latency.
- DMA stall fraction measured from /proc stats and kernel debug counters.

Notable observations
1) Short soft window (50ms) substantially reduced short-lived re-evictions: eviction_rate dropped ~28% vs baseline in burst scenario, reuse_rate rose 4–6% for chat flows, P99 token latency improved 12–18ms on average. NVMe IOPS spike magnitude reduced ~22%.
2) Medium window (200ms) further reduced eviction_rate (~44% vs baseline) but introduced a measurable degradation in steady-state reuse for high-concurrency constrained nodes on long-running runs: degradation_factor ~0.03 (i.e., 3% lower hit-rate for non-bursty periods) and small unit-cost increase (~2% more host memory timeslices).
3) Soft-adaptive mode provided the best tradeoff: when a burst detector (short-term eviction_rate slope > threshold AND NVMe IOPS rising) triggered, we extended windows to soak burst. This mode matched P99 improvements of soft-200ms for bursts while avoiding steady-state degradation — net reuse_rate matched baseline outside bursts and improved during them.
4) Pageback storms are highly correlated with simultaneous expiry across many small partitions (hot-window fragmentation). Soft windows reduce the chance of simultaneous expiry by desynchronizing eviction events. We see a lower covariance of eviction timestamps across tenant partitions under soft configs.
5) Memory-bandwidth contention still occurs even with preserved KV residency: when reuse-rate increases and many tokens request adjacent KV pages, per-channel bank saturation spikes. Soft windows don't solve bank saturation; they reduce the IO writeback spike but can increase concurrent read bandwidth if working set remains resident.

Experiment notes and anomaly logs
- Observed an outlier run where soft-200ms + burst increased P50 slightly (~3ms) due to excessive pinning in streams with poor reuse_signal calibration; root cause was reuse_signal smoothing too long for embed-heavy flows. Ticket created: SERV-3247.
- Kernel-level DMA stall counters rose ~1.6x in a scenario where host CPU scheduling delayed prefetch worker threads; this amplified NVMe latency during a prolonged burst. Patch PR #4972 addresses worker scheduling priority.

Policy implications / recommended defaults
- Default rollout: enable soft-adaptive mode with conservative base window of 20ms. Enable extension up to 300ms under burst detection (eviction_rate slope + NVMe IOPS threshold). This captures short transients while avoiding steady degradation.
- reuse_signal gating: do not treat window as a pure time-based TTL; only extend window for entries whose reuse_signal > 0.2. This prevents long-lived, cold entries from holding memory.
- Partition randomization: introduce a small jitter on window start per-partition (2–10ms) to break alignment of eviction across tenants.

Operational runbook (quick)
1) Detection: if P99 tokens > baseline P99 + 20ms AND NVMe IOPS burst observed, incrementally raise soft window extension factor by 1.5x on affected nodes and monitor eviction_rate and reuse_rate for 10 minutes.
2) Rollback: if steady-state reuse_rate drops >5% after 30 minutes, revert to base window and file a calibration task for reuse_signal.
3) Emergency pinning: if pageback_iops > 2x steady-state and P99 > 2x baseline, enable emergency pin for top-K hot keys for 1s to avoid repeated paging. Use sparingly — costs increase.

Implementation notes for eng team
- Reuse signal metrics: add moving-exponential-weighted metric per-key-class with decay tau=150ms. Emit reuse_signal in telemetry as reuse_signal_v0 for initial rollout.
- Soft window state: small additional per-entry metadata (expiry_deadline, soft_guard_flag) — aim to keep on-heap memory overhead < 8 bytes per entry by compressing flags.
- Burst detector heuristic: (d_eviction/dt > alpha && nvme_iops_recent > beta) where alpha = 0.12 evictions/sec slope per partition, beta = 1.3x steady-state IOPS.
- Telemetry: add cov(eviction_ts) across partitions metric to detect desynchronization benefits.

Open questions / experiments to run next
- Quantify long-term cost tradeoffs on Dedicated nodes with tight capacity commitments (simulate reserve-bound workloads for 72h). We need to measure billing-equivalent token cost delta.
- Interaction with quantized model KV layout: do different KV encodings have different reuse_signal distributions? Run tests with 4-bit vs 8-bit quant layouts.
- Bank-aware pinning: can we prioritize residency for entries mapped across different memory channels to reduce single-channel saturation? Preliminary idea: prefer pinning keys whose physical pages scatter across banks. Needs allocator exposure.
- Multi-tenant fairness: measure whether tenants with differing traffic patterns gain/lose when soft windows are globally enabled.

Action items & owners
- Implement soft-adaptive prototype + telemetry (Sofia) -> branch: soft-window-prototype (gh pr #4972 linked).
- Add reuse_signal EWM metric and telemetry schema (Devon).
- Run 72h reserved-capacity simulation for Dedicated workloads (Ravi).
- Create customer-facing summary for CS for what to expect during rollout (Amira).

Notes to self
- Keep parameter names stable: use soft_eviction_window_ms and soft_window_max_extension_ms in config surfaces.
- Validate telemetry units (ms vs seconds) in console dashboards.

Appendix (short logs)
- Baseline burst run (2026-02-20 02:12Z): eviction_rate = 4.3k/s node, nvme_iops = 18.2k, P99 token = 210ms.
- soft-50ms run same window: eviction_rate = 3.1k/s, nvme_iops = 14.1k, P99 token = 196ms.
- soft-adaptive median across 10 runs: eviction_rate reduction 35%, NVMe IOPS reduction 26%, P99 improvement 15–30ms depending on mix.

If you want, I can convert this into a short slide deck for the eng sync (2–3 slides) or a Confluence page with more structured telemetry graphs (need raw trace links).
